newsitem.title: USA: US budget deal raises deficit then reaches surplus.
newsitem.headline: US budget deal raises deficit then reaches surplus.

text.p: The budget agreement reached between the White House and congressional leaders would raise the deficit in fiscal 1998 to $91 billion from an expected $67 billion this year, the Senate Budget Committee said Friday.
Under the five-year budget plan, the deficit would then level off in fiscal 1999 at $90 billion, slip to $83 billion in 2000 and then to $53 billion in 2001.
In 2002 there would be a $1 billion surplus, followed by surpluses in each of the next five years, ending in a $34 billion surplus in 2007, the committee said.
Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, was asked about the fact that more than 60 percent of the deficit reduction occurs in the last two years of the budget plan.
He replied: "When I look at what we did, I don't believe there's any way that you can do much better."

With tax cuts starting in the first year and Medicare savings increasing in the later years of the plan, "I am satisfied that this is a good ratio and if we enforce it we'll come out just fine," Domenici told reporters.
